items: **Existing conversation:** Madeline replied to **Tunahan** on LinkedIn (logged Oct 20, 2026) and invited an email. That is the only confirmed link.

**Same problem, two ends:** NxGen screens couples for inherited recessive disease; PhiTech (Saliha and Tunahan) builds tools to **diagnose rare genetic disease** from DNA and RNA. Same patient journey.
**Hereditary cancer:** NxGen runs a 32-gene NCCN panel with pre- and post-test counseling; PhiTech's site names hereditary cancer as a G&M focus and its 2026 round funds cancer R&D.

No shared school, employer, country or conference found on the public web. Saliha and Tunahan trained at Boğaziçi University and taught at Gebze Technical University (Türkiye); Tunahan's postdoc was in the Netherlands.

lead_with.title: After the screen, the diagnosis
lead_with.text: NxGen's carrier screens flag at-risk couples. When a child is affected, DNA-only testing diagnoses **under 40%** of rare-disease cases (per PhiTech's 2026 funding coverage). G&M adds **RNA-seq plus AI gene prioritization** — PhiTech claims **up to 30% better diagnostic yield**.

lead_with.title: Help for the counselors
lead_with.text: Madeline runs the team that explains results. G&M is a web-based **decision-support tool** that links variants to functional (RNA) evidence — pitch it as clearer, evidence-backed reports for her counselors, not as more lab work.

lead_with.title: Make it forwardable
lead_with.text: She is a manager, not the buyer. Send a short note plus a one-page summary she can pass to **CEO Alan Mack** or **CCO Greg Richard**, and ask who owns variant interpretation.

company.text: NxGen MDx (NxGen MDx, LLC) is a private molecular diagnostics lab at 801 Broadway Ave NW, Grand Rapids, MI, founded in 2012 by **Alan Mack**, still CEO. It started in Grand Valley State University's health-sciences incubator. It sells NGS carrier screening (Super Panel and Early Advantage Panel, marketed as pan-ethnic), whole-genome NIPS, a 32-gene NCCN hereditary cancer panel and PCR infection tests, mostly through OB/GYNs, under its "NatalCare" philosophy. In **Nov 2025** it published a 400-patient retrospective study: NIPT plus the 147-condition Super Panel found all 400 carrier couples, against an estimated 63 for a 14-condition single-gene NIPT.

industry.title: Expanded carrier screening is the standard
industry.text: ACMG recommends offering **Tier 3** carrier screening (a 113-gene set) to all pregnant patients and those planning pregnancy. NxGen's broad panels are built on this trend.

industry.title: Single-gene NIPT under fire
industry.text: NxGen's Nov 2025 release cites ACOG, ACMG and SMFM statements that single-gene cfDNA screening is not recommended or not yet proven. Broad panels and confirmatory diagnosis are the line it sells.

industry.title: RNA-seq enters rare-disease diagnosis
industry.text: At ASHG 2025, Baylor Genetics reported that RNA-seq **reclassified half of eligible variants** and supported a diagnosis in **24%** of Undiagnosed Diseases Network patients. US labs are adding transcriptomics — the core of PhiTech's G&M.

talking_points: When a Super Panel finds an at-risk couple and a baby is later affected, where do those families go for diagnostic testing today?
How much of your counselors' time goes to explaining variants of uncertain significance?
Who owns variant interpretation and bioinformatics at NxGen — in-house or outsourced?
Has NxGen looked at RNA-seq to resolve uncertain or splicing variants, for example in the hereditary cancer panel?
Would a small pilot — a few unresolved cases re-analysed on G&M — be useful to show the team?
Who should see this besides you — Alan Mack, Greg Richard or lab operations?
